questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lenticels are absent in
questions.solution:
Lenticels are lens-shaped openings formed during secondary growth in the periderm. They are present in the bark of old stems, older roots of dicot flowering plants, and the pericarp of woody fruits. They facilitate the exchange of gases between the internal tissues and the external atmosphere.

Leaves do not possess lenticels; instead, they have stomata for gaseous exchange. Therefore, lenticels are absent in leaves.

Answer: leaves

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which animal belongs to group Hyalobatidae?
questions.solution:
Gibbons belong to the family Hylobatidae, which are commonly known as lesser apes.

Gorillas, chimpanzees, and orangutans belong to the family Hominidae, which are known as great apes.

Answer: Gibbons

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following animal phyla show closed blood vascular system apart from vertebrates?
questions.solution:
In a closed circulatory system, blood is confined to vessels and is distinct from the interstitial fluid.

Annelids possess a closed circulatory system where blood circulates through a continuous network of vessels.

Most molluscs have an open circulatory system, but higher molluscs, specifically cephalopods (such as squids and octopuses), have a closed circulatory system to support their active lifestyle.

Arthropods and echinoderms have an open circulatory system.

Thus, apart from vertebrates, annelids and higher molluscs exhibit a closed blood vascular system.

Answer: Annelids and higher Molluscs

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In Annelids like earthworm and nereis, majority of gaseous exchange takes place through-----------.
questions.solution:
In Annelids such as earthworms and Nereis, there are no specialized respiratory organs like lungs or gills for the majority of gaseous exchange.

They respire through their moist body surface (skin). The skin is kept moist by the secretion of mucus and coelomic fluid, which facilitates the diffusion of oxygen into the blood and carbon dioxide out of it. This process is known as cutaneous respiration.

Book lungs are found in arachnids, tracheal tubes in insects, and book gills in horseshoe crabs.

Answer: moist skin

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The process by which the diploid oocyst of Plasmodium forms large number of haploid sporozoites through meiosis in the gut wall of female anopheles is called ---------.
questions.solution:
ed sporogony.

Schizogony refers to the asexual multiplication that occurs in the human host (liver and red blood cells).

Gamogony is the formation of gametes.

Syngamy is the fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote.

Answer: sporogony

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which group has more diversity of known species of organisms from the following?
questions.solution:
According to global biodiversity estimates, animals are the most diverse group of organisms, constituting more than $70\%$ of all recorded species.

Plants (including algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise no more than $22\%$ of the total species.

Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than $70\%$ of the total animal species.

Therefore, animals have the highest diversity of known species among the given groups.

Answer: Animals

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Pilot plantation programmes using Miyawaki pattern in various districts of Maharashtra are run by the State Forest Department and -----------------.
questions.solution:
The Miyawaki method of afforestation is a technique pioneered by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, which helps build dense, native forests in a short time.

In Maharashtra, pilot plantation programmes using the Miyawaki pattern in various districts are jointly run by the State Forest Department and the Social Forestry Department.

Answer: Social Forestry Department

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of following group includes reducing sugars?
questions.solution:
Reducing sugars are carbohydrates that contain a free aldehyde or ketone group and can reduce Fehling's solution and Tollens' reagent.

All monosaccharides, such as glucose, fructose, and galactose, are reducing sugars.

Disaccharides in which the anomeric carbon of at least one monosaccharide unit is free are also reducing sugars. Examples include maltose and lactose.

In sucrose, the glycosidic bond is formed between the anomeric carbon of glucose (C1) and the anomeric carbon of fructose (C2). Since both anomeric carbons are involved in the linkage, there is no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group, making sucrose a non-reducing sugar.

Therefore, the group containing only reducing sugars is Glucose, Lactose, and Maltose.

Answer: Glucose, Lactose, Maltose

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: All of the following are conjugated proteins EXCEPT
questions.solution:
Proteins are broadly classified into simple, conjugated, and derived proteins based on their structural composition and the products of their hydrolysis.

Simple proteins are composed entirely of amino acids and yield only amino acids upon complete hydrolysis. Histones are a well-known example of simple proteins; they are highly basic proteins rich in arginine and lysine residues that associate with DNA in eukaryotic chromatin.

Conjugated proteins contain a protein part combined with a non-protein component called a prosthetic group. Haemoglobin is a conjugated protein (specifically a chromoprotein or metalloprotein) that contains a protein globin bound to an iron-containing heme group. Mucin is also a conjugated protein (specifically a glycoprotein) where carbohydrate chains are covalently linked to the protein backbone. Heparin is a glycosaminoglycan that exists biologically attached to a core protein to form a proteoglycan, which is classified as a conjugated protein structure.

Since histones are classified strictly as simple proteins and do not contain any non-protein prosthetic group, they are not conjugated proteins.

Answer: Histones

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The organic compounds that are tightly attached to the protein part of an enzyme to make them catalatically active are called -------------------.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT Biology, cofactors are non-protein constituents bound to the enzyme to make it catalytically active.

There are three kinds of cofactors: prosthetic groups, co-enzymes, and metal ions.

Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme (the protein part of the enzyme).

Co-enzymes are also organic compounds, but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient.

Therefore, the organic compounds tightly attached to the protein part of an enzyme are called prosthetic groups.

Answer: prosthetic groups

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which amino acids are synthesized from intermediates of Krebs cycle like alpha-ketoglutarate and oxaloacetate?
questions.solution:
The intermediates of the Krebs cycle serve as precursors for the synthesis of various amino acids through transamination reactions.

$\alpha$-ketoglutarate undergoes reductive amination or transamination to form glutamic acid (glutamate).

Oxaloacetate undergoes transamination, accepting an amino group from glutamate, to form aspartic acid (aspartate).

Therefore, glutamic acid and aspartic acid are the amino acids synthesized from $\alpha$-ketoglutarate and oxaloacetate, respectively.

Answer: Glutamic acid and aspartic acid

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Enzyme)		List II
(Reaction catalyzed)
(A). Alcohol dehydrogenase(I). Transfer of certain groups between two molecules
(B). Sucrase(II). Oxidation and reduction reactions
(C). Glucokinase(III). Structural rearrangements within a molecule
(D). Racemases(IV). Hydrolytic reactions
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Alcohol dehydrogenase belongs to the class of oxidoreductases, which catalyze oxidation and reduction reactions. Thus, (A) matches with (II).

Sucrase is a hydrolase enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose. Thus, (B) matches with (IV).

Glucokinase is a transferase enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group from ATP to glucose. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

Racemases are isomerase enzymes that catalyze structural rearrangements within a molecule to convert one stereoisomer into another. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which enzyme in the midgut of insect is instrumental in the release of core toxic fragments from bacterial spores ingested by it?
questions.solution:
Bacillus thuringiensis produces proteinaceous toxins in an inactive form called protoxins.

When an insect ingests these spores or crystals, the alkaline pH of the insect's midgut solubilizes the crystals.

Subsequently, midgut proteinases (proteases) cleave the inactive protoxin into its active core toxic fragments.

These active toxins bind to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis, eventually leading to the death of the insect.

Answer: Proteinase

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The scientists who earned Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1989 for the discovery of Ribozymes are ---------.
questions.solution:
Sidney Altman and Thomas R. Cech were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in $1989$ for their independent discoveries that RNA can act as a biological catalyst. These catalytic RNA molecules are known as ribozymes.

Oparin and Haldane proposed the theory of chemical evolution.

Crick and Orgel were involved in proposing the RNA world hypothesis.

Urey and Miller provided experimental evidence for the chemical origin of life.

Answer: Altman and Cech

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement with respect to the respiratory system.
options: The oropharynx is a common passage for food and air.
Larynx contains vocal cords for producing sound.
The trachea is supported by 'C' shaped rings of cartilage.
The trachea is internally lined by simple squamous epithelium.
questions.solution:
The pharynx is the common passage for food and air, with the oropharynx being a part of it.

The larynx is a cartilaginous box which helps in sound production and is hence called the sound box.

The trachea is a straight tube extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity. The trachea, primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete ('C' shaped) cartilaginous rings.

The trachea is internally lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, not simple squamous epithelium. Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of alveoli where it forms a diffusion boundary.

Answer: The trachea is internally lined by simple squamous epithelium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The volume of air remaining in the lungs and the dead space even after maximum expiration is ----------ml.
questions.solution:
ion is called the Residual Volume (RV).

The average value of Residual Volume in a healthy human adult is $1100$ mL to $1200$ mL.

Other respiratory volumes are:
Tidal Volume (TV) $\approx 500$ mL
Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) $\approx 1000$ to $1100$ mL
Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) $\approx 2500$ to $3000$ mL

Answer: 1100-1200

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements about the oxygen dissociation curve.
Statement (I): The relationship between HbO_2$ saturation and oxygen tension (ppO_2$) is called oxygen dissociation curve.
Statement (II): Oxygen dissociation curve shifts towards the right due to decrease in H$^+$ concentration and decrease in temperature.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct. The oxygen dissociation curve is a graphical representation of the relationship between the partial pressure of oxygen (p$O_2$) and the percentage saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen. \\ \\ Statement (II) is incorrect. The oxygen dissociation curve shifts to the right when there is a decrease in oxygen affinity of hemoglobin. This occurs due to an increase in H$^+$ concentration (decrease in pH), an increase in partial pressure of CO_2$ (pCO_2$), and an increase in temperature. A decrease in H$^+$ concentration and a decrease in temperature would shift the curve to the left.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Type of chromosome)		List II
(Shape of chromosome)
(A). Acrocentric(I). i shaped
(B). Metacentric(II). L shaped
(C). Telocentric(III). j shaped
(D). Submetacentric(IV). V shaped
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Based on the position of the centromere, chromosomes are classified into four types, and their shapes during anaphase are as follows:

Metacentric chromosomes have the centromere in the middle, forming two equal arms. They appear V-shaped during anaphase. Thus, (B) matches (IV).

Submetacentric chromosomes have the centromere slightly away from the middle, forming one shorter arm and one longer arm. They appear L-shaped during anaphase. Thus, (D) matches (II).

Acrocentric chromosomes have the centromere situated close to its end, forming one extremely short and one very long arm. They appear j-shaped during anaphase. Thus, (A) matches (III).

Telocentric chromosomes have a terminal centromere. They appear i-shaped during anaphase. Thus, (C) matches (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: ------------------- constitutes a large regional terrestrial unit delimited by a specific climatic zone having major vegetation zone and the associated fauna.
questions.solution:
A biome is defined as a large regional terrestrial unit delimited by a specific climatic zone having a major vegetation zone and the associated fauna.

It represents the largest recognizable subdivision of the terrestrial ecosystem, characterized by its climate and dominant plant life.

Examples of biomes include deserts, tropical rainforests, tundras, and grasslands.

Answer: Biome

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The process of degradation of humus by soil microbes to release inorganic nutrients is called as --------------.
questions.solution:
Decomposition involves several steps: fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, and mineralisation.

Humification leads to the accumulation of a dark-coloured amorphous substance called humus that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.

The humus is further degraded by some microbes and the release of inorganic nutrients occurs by the process known as mineralisation.

Answer: mineralisation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements related to the ecological pyramid.
Statement (I): Ecological pyramid assumes a simple food chain, something that never exists in nature.
Statement (II): Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids as they do not play any vital role in the ecosystem.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct because ecological pyramids assume a simple food chain, which almost never exists in nature, and they do not accommodate a food web.

Statement (II) is incorrect. Although saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids, they play a very vital role in the ecosystem by acting as decomposers and helping in nutrient cycling.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which are the pioneer species in hydrarch succession of plants?
questions.solution:
Hydrarch succession takes place in wetter areas and the successional series progress from hydric to mesic conditions.

The pioneer species in primary succession in water are small phytoplanktons.

These phytoplanktons are replaced with time by free-floating angiosperms, then by rooted hydrophytes, sedges, grasses, and finally trees.

Crustose lichens are the pioneer species in xerarch succession on bare rocks.

Answer: Small phytoplanktons

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT favour speciation?
options: Less climatic changes throughout the year
questions.solution:
Speciation is generally a function of time. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, providing a long evolutionary time for species diversification.

Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant, and predictable. Such constant environments promote niche specialisation and lead to greater species diversity.

There is more solar energy available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity and indirectly to greater diversity.

Drastic seasonal variations are characteristic of temperate regions and do not favour speciation or species diversity.

Answer: Drastic seasonal variations

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Populations with --------------- individuals have greater chances of genetic drift.
questions.solution:
Genetic drift refers to the random fluctuations in allele frequencies from one generation to the next. It occurs in all populations, but its effects are much more pronounced in small populations. In large populations, random variations tend to average out, keeping allele frequencies relatively stable. In contrast, small populations are highly susceptible to genetic drift, which can lead to the rapid loss or fixation of alleles purely by chance.

Among the given options, $5000-10000$ represents the smallest population size. Therefore, a population with $5000-10000$ individuals has the greatest chance of experiencing significant genetic drift.

Answer: 5000-10000.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The natural selection in which more number of individuals acquire peripheral character value at both ends of the distribution curve is called ----------------- selection.
questions.solution:
Natural selection can be of three main types based on its effect on the distribution of traits in a population:

Stabilizing selection: More individuals acquire the mean character value, and variation is reduced.

Directional selection: More individuals acquire a value other than the mean character value, shifting the peak in one direction.

Disruptive selection: More individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve, leading to a bimodal distribution where extreme traits are favored over intermediate ones.

Therefore, the selection described in the question is disruptive selection.

Answer: disruptive

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements related to sympatric speciation:
Statement (I): Formation of species within single population without geographical isolation is sympatric speciation.
Statement (II): Migration of individuals is helpful in sympatric speciation.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Sympatric speciation is the process through which new species evolve from a single ancestral species while inhabiting the same geographic region. It occurs without any geographical isolation, making Statement (I) correct.

Migration of individuals leads to gene flow between populations or subpopulations, which tends to homogenize the gene pool and prevent the reproductive isolation necessary for speciation. Therefore, migration is a barrier to sympatric speciation rather than being helpful, making Statement (II) incorrect.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Immune cells)		List II
(Functions)
(A). Plasma cells(I). Bind to infected cell and secrete perforins
(B). Helper T-cells(II). Produce specialized glycoproteins, called antibodies
(C). Cytotoxic T-cells(III). Engulf invading pathogens and process the antigens
(D). Antigen presenting cells(IV). Stimulation of B-lymphocytes, macrophages
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Plasma cells are effector B-lymphocytes that produce and secrete large amounts of antibodies, which are specialized glycoproteins. Thus, (A) matches with (II).

Helper T-cells secrete cytokines that stimulate the proliferation and differentiation of B-lymphocytes and activate macrophages. Thus, (B) matches with (IV).

Cytotoxic T-cells recognize infected cells and secrete perforins and granzymes to induce apoptosis in the target cells. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

Antigen presenting cells (such as macrophages and dendritic cells) engulf pathogens, process their antigens, and present them on their surface using MHC molecules to activate T-cells. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Identify the CORRECT pair of vector borne diseases.
questions.solution:
Vector-borne diseases are transmitted by vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, or fleas.

Dengue is transmitted by the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito.

Filariasis is transmitted by the bite of an infected Culex mosquito.

Typhoid and amoebiasis are transmitted through contaminated food and water.

Ringworm is a fungal infection transmitted through direct contact.

Pneumonia is transmitted through droplet infection.

Therefore, Dengue and filariasis are both vector-borne diseases.

Answer: Dengue and filariasis

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements related to drugs abuse:
Statement (I): Excessive dosage of cocaine causes extreme happiness, irritability, paranoia etc.
Statement (II): A drug like heroin obtained from Cannabis sativa is used as depressant as it slows down the activity of body.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is incorrect. According to NCERT, cocaine has a potent stimulating action on the central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria (extreme happiness) and increased energy at normal doses. However, an excessive dosage of cocaine causes hallucinations.

Statement (II) is incorrect. Heroin is a depressant and slows down body functions, but it is obtained from the acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant (Papaver somniferum). Cannabis sativa is the source of cannabinoids (such as marijuana, hashish, charas, and ganja), not heroin.

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fertilizin receptor proteins necessary for attraction of sperms to the egg in mammals are present on ---------.
questions.solution:
Fertilizin is a glycoprotein that acts as a sperm receptor. In mammals, these receptor proteins (such as ZP3) are present on the zona pellucida, which is the thick, transparent, extracellular layer surrounding the mammalian ovum. The interaction between fertilizin on the zona pellucida and antifertilizin on the sperm ensures species-specific fertilization.

Answer: zona pellucida

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: How many eggs are released by a human female in the time period of about 32 years between menarche and menopause?
questions.solution:
A human female typically releases one egg per menstrual cycle.

The average length of a menstrual cycle is $28$ days.

Number of menstrual cycles in a year = $\dfrac{365}{28} \approx 13$.

Therefore, approximately $13$ eggs are released per year.

Total number of eggs released in $32$ years = $32 \times 13 = 416$.

Answer: $416$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements with respect to gastrulation:
Statement (I): The cells of epiblast towards the blastocoel contribute in the formation of yolk sac.
Statement (II): The cells of epiblast take part in the formation of third germinal layer, the mesoderm.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is incorrect because the cells of the hypoblast (not epiblast) migrate towards the blastocoel and line its inner surface to form the primary yolk sac.

Statement (II) is correct because during gastrulation, cells of the epiblast migrate through the primitive streak to form the intraembryonic mesoderm and embryonic endoderm, while the remaining epiblast cells form the ectoderm. Thus, the epiblast is the source of all three germ layers, including the mesoderm.

Answer: Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Which of these developments occurs during the 1$^{st}$ trimester of pregnancy?
(A). Arms, hands, fingers, feet, toes are formed.
(B). Baby's movements can be easily felt by the mother.
(C). Foetus can open and close mouth and fists.
(D). The CNS is developing, working of the excretory and circulatory systems begins.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The first trimester of pregnancy corresponds to the first 12 weeks. Let us evaluate the given statements:

Statement (A) is correct. By the end of the second month of pregnancy, which is within the first trimester, the foetus develops limbs and digits, including arms, hands, fingers, feet, and toes.

Statement (B) is incorrect. The first movements of the foetus are typically felt by the mother during the fifth month, which falls in the second trimester.

Statement (C) is correct. By the end of the first trimester, most of the major organ systems are formed, and the foetus begins to show early reflex actions such as opening and closing fists and mouth.

Statement (D) is correct. The development of the central nervous system starts early in the first trimester, and the circulatory and excretory systems begin to function as major organ systems are established.

Therefore, statements (A), (C), and (D) represent developments during the first trimester.

Answer: (A), (C) and (D) only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Microbial source of antibiotic terramycin is -------------.
questions.solution:
The antibiotic terramycin, also known chemically as oxytetracycline, is naturally produced by the soil bacterium Streptomyces rimosus.

The other microorganisms listed produce different antibiotics:
Streptomyces venezuelae is the source of chloramphenicol.
Streptomyces griseus is the source of streptomycin.
Streptomyces erythreus is the source of erythromycin.

Therefore, the correct microbial source for terramycin is Streptomyces rimosus.

Answer: Streptomyces rimosus

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: How many electrons and ATP are required for the biological fixation of a molecule of nitrogen to form ammonia?
questions.solution:
The biological nitrogen fixation is catalyzed by the enzyme nitrogenase. The overall reaction for the reduction of one molecule of nitrogen ($N_2$) to two molecules of ammonia ($NH_3$) is given by:

$N_2 + 8e^- + 8H^+ + 16ATP \rightarrow 2NH_3 + H_2 + 16ADP + 16P_i$

From the balanced equation, the fixation of one molecule of nitrogen requires $8$ electrons and $16$ ATP molecules.

Answer: 8 and 16 respectively

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following groups has all three micro-elements?
questions.solution:
Macronutrients are generally present in plant tissues in large amounts (in excess of $10 \text{ mmole kg}^{-1}$ of dry matter). The macronutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur, potassium, calcium and magnesium.

Micronutrients or trace elements are needed in very small amounts (less than $10 \text{ mmole kg}^{-1}$ of dry matter). These include iron, manganese, copper, molybdenum, zinc, boron, chlorine and nickel.

Analyzing the given options:
Magnesium (Mg), Potassium (K), Sulphur (S), and Calcium (Ca) are macronutrients.
Therefore, the groups in the first, third, and fourth options contain macronutrients.

Zinc (Zn) and Copper (Cu) are micronutrients, and Silicon (Si) is a beneficial trace element required by some higher plants. Since it does not contain any macronutrients, this is the most appropriate choice.

Answer: Zinc, Copper, Silicon

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Meselson and Stahl proved the semi-conservative nature of DNA replication using the isotope ___.
questions.solution:
Meselson and Stahl performed an experiment in 1958 to prove the semi-conservative nature of DNA replication.

They grew E. coli in a medium containing $^{15}\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ ($^{15}\text{N}$ is the heavy isotope of nitrogen) for many generations. The result was that $^{15}\text{N}$ was incorporated into newly synthesized DNA (as well as other nitrogen-containing compounds). This heavy DNA molecule could be distinguished from the normal DNA by centrifugation in a cesium chloride (CsCl) density gradient.

Therefore, the isotope used was $^{15}\text{N}$.

Answer: $^{15}\text{N}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the chromosomes, DNA is associated with histone and non-histone proteins. This was reported in 1974 by -----------------.
questions.solution:
In 1974, R. Kornberg reported that in chromosomes, DNA is associated with histone and non-histone proteins to form the basic structural unit of chromatin, which is known as the nucleosome.

F.H.C. Crick co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA in 1953.

F. Miescher discovered nucleic acids (nuclein) in 1869.

F. Griffith discovered the transforming principle in 1928.

Answer: R. Kornberg

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement with respect to coding strand.
options: It is also known as sense strand.
The terminator is located at 3' end of coding strand.
The nucleotide sequence of this strand is the same as in RNA, except that RNA contains uracil in place of thymine.
The nucleotide sequence of this strand is the same as in the template strand with 3' \rightarrow  5' polarity.
questions.solution:
The coding strand is the DNA strand whose base sequence corresponds to the base sequence of the RNA transcript produced, with thymine replaced by uracil. It is also known as the sense strand or non-template strand.

The promoter is located towards the 5' end (upstream) of the structural gene with respect to the coding strand, while the terminator is located towards the 3' end (downstream) of the coding strand.

The nucleotide sequence of the coding strand is complementary to the template strand, not the same as it. Therefore, the statement that its sequence is the same as the template strand is incorrect.

Answer: The nucleotide sequence of this strand is the same as in the template strand with 3' \rightarrow 5' polarity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following related to HGP.
options: HGP is a multinational research project to determine the genomic structure of humans.
The human genome project was initiated in 1990.
HGP was co-ordinated by the US department of biotechnology and life sciences.
questions.solution:
The Human Genome Project (HGP) was a multinational research project aimed at determining the genomic structure of humans.

The project was initiated in the year 1990 and was successfully completed in 2003.

The HGP was closely coordinated by the US Department of Energy and the National Institutes of Health (NIH), not by the US department of biotechnology and life sciences.

Therefore, the statement claiming it was coordinated by the US department of biotechnology and life sciences is incorrect.

Answer: HGP was co-ordinated by the US department of biotechnology and life sciences.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: As in rDNA technology, in DNA fingerprinting, also, all the following techniques are used EXCEPT:
questions.solution:
DNA fingerprinting involves the isolation of DNA, digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases, separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis, Southern blotting, hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe, and detection by autoradiography.

Cloning vector plasmids are used in recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology to carry and replicate foreign DNA inside a host cell. They are not required or used in the process of DNA fingerprinting.

Answer: Cloning vector plasmids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which phase of plant growth, the rate of growth slows down and comes to a steady state?
questions.solution:
The period of plant growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic (cell division), elongation (cell enlargement), and maturation.

During the phase of cell division, cells are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei.

During the phase of cell elongation, there is increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition, leading to a rapid increase in size.

During the phase of cell maturation, cells attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications. In this phase, the rate of growth slows down and eventually comes to a steady state.

Answer: Phase of cell maturation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Identify the INCORRECT statement about gibberellins.
options: It promotes bolting in beet and cabbage.
It causes epinasty of leaves and flowers.
It promotes seed germination in cereals.
It breaks dormancy of seed and hastens germination.
questions.solution:
Gibberellins are plant growth regulators that promote stem elongation, bolting in rosette plants like beet and cabbage, and seed germination by breaking dormancy and stimulating the synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes in cereals.

Epinasty, which is the downward bending of leaves and flowers due to greater growth on the upper side, is primarily caused by ethylene, not gibberellins.

Therefore, the statement that gibberellins cause epinasty of leaves and flowers is incorrect.

Answer: It causes epinasty of leaves and flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: If the dark period is interrupted even by a flash of light, plants like tobacco and soybean ______
options: cannot be made to flower again.
questions.solution:
Tobacco and soybean are short-day plants.

Short-day plants require a continuous and uninterrupted dark period exceeding a critical duration to initiate flowering.

If the dark period is interrupted even by a brief flash of light, the phytochrome system is reset, which inhibits the flowering process.

Therefore, these plants will not flower.

Answer: will not flower.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A sickle-cell carrier man marries a woman who is carrier for sickle-cell anaemia. What are the chances of having carrier children?
options: All the children will be carriers.
None of them will be carriers.
questions.solution:
Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder.

Let the normal allele be $Hb^A$ and the sickle-cell allele be $Hb^S$.

The genotype of the carrier man is $Hb^A Hb^S$ and the carrier woman is $Hb^A Hb^S$.

The cross between them is $Hb^A Hb^S \times Hb^A Hb^S$.

The possible genotypes of the offspring are:
$25\%Hb^A Hb^A$ (Normal)
$50\%Hb^A Hb^S$ (Carrier)
$25\%Hb^S Hb^S$ (Affected)

The chances of having carrier children is $50\%$.

Answer: $50\%$ of them will be carriers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A pea plant with genotype RrYy is crossed with another pea plant with genotype rryy. What will be the number of phenotypes obtained by this cross?
questions.solution:
The given cross is between a dihybrid plant (RrYy) and a homozygous recessive plant (rryy).

This is a dihybrid test cross.

The plant with genotype RrYy produces four types of gametes: RY, Ry, rY, and ry.

The plant with genotype rryy produces only one type of gamete: ry.

The offspring produced from this cross will have the following genotypes and phenotypes:

RrYy : Round Yellow
Rryy : Round Green
rrYy : Wrinkled Yellow
rryy : Wrinkled Green

Thus, four different phenotypes are obtained in a ratio of $1:1:1:1$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which one of the following is a symptom of Klinefelter's Syndrome?
questions.solution:
Klinefelter's syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of 47, XXY.

Individuals with this syndrome have overall masculine development, but feminine characteristics are also expressed. One of the prominent symptoms is the development of breasts, which is known as Gynaecomastia.

Webbed neck, broad shield-shaped chest, and lower posterior hair line are symptoms associated with Turner's syndrome (45, XO).

Answer: Gynaecomastia

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A normal woman whose father was colourblind is married to a normal man, (assuming equal distribution of female gametes), then _________.
options: $50\%$ of their sons will be colourblind.
All the sons will be colourblind.
All the sons will be normal.
$75\%$ of the sons will be colourblind.
questions.solution:
Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait.

Let $X^C$ be the normal allele and $X^c$ be the allele for colour blindness.

The woman's father was colourblind ($X^c Y$), so he passed the $X^c$ chromosome to her. Since she is normal, her genotype is $X^C X^c$ (carrier).

The normal man has the genotype $X^C Y$.

A cross between the carrier woman ($X^C X^c$) and the normal man ($X^C Y$) produces the following offspring:

Daughters: $X^C X^C$ (normal) and $X^C X^c$ (normal carrier).

Sons: $X^C Y$ (normal) and $X^c Y$ (colourblind).

Since the sons receive their X chromosome from the mother, who produces $X^C$ and $X^c$ gametes in equal proportions, $50\%$ of the sons will be normal and $50\%$ will be colourblind.

Answer: $50\%$ of their sons will be colourblind.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Identify the hormone releasing Intra Uterine Device from the following.
questions.solution:
Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) are classified into three main types:

Non-medicated IUDs: Lippes loop.

Copper releasing IUDs: CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375.

Hormone releasing IUDs: Progestasert, LNG-20.

Therefore, LNG-20 is a hormone releasing IUD.

Answer: LNG-20

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which cytochrome acts as a mobile electron carrier, transferring electrons between complex III and IV during ETS?
questions.solution:
Cytochrome c is a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane.

It acts as a mobile carrier for the transfer of electrons between complex III (cytochrome b$c_1$ complex) and complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase complex).

Therefore, cytochrome c is the correct mobile electron carrier.

Answer: Cytochrome c

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which enzyme is responsible for phosphorylation of glucose with ATP?
questions.solution:
The first step of glycolysis involves the phosphorylation of glucose to form glucose-6-phosphate.

This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme hexokinase, which uses ATP as the phosphate donor.

Phosphofructokinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

Aldolase catalyzes the cleavage of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into two three-carbon sugars.

Phosphohexose isomerase catalyzes the isomerization of glucose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate.

Answer: Hexokinase

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: How many glucose molecules are utilized if the cell produces 68 pyruvic acid molecules during glycolysis?
questions.solution:
During glycolysis, one molecule of glucose is broken down to produce two molecules of pyruvic acid.

Number of glucose molecules utilized = $\dfrac{\text{Number of pyruvic acid molecules produced}}{2}$

Number of glucose molecules utilized = $\dfrac{68}{2} = 34$

Answer: $34$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During aerobic respiration, the total number of ATP formed from one glucose molecule through substrate level phosphorylation is ----------------------.
questions.solution:
SIn aerobic respiration, ATP is synthesized from a single molecule of glucose through two distinct pathways: substrate-level phosphorylation and oxidative phosphorylation.

In the classical balance sheet of aerobic respiration, the complete oxidation of one glucose molecule yields a net total of $38$ ATP molecules. This total consists of $34$ ATP molecules produced via oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain and $4$ ATP molecules produced via substrate-level phosphorylation.

The breakdown of ATP formed directly by substrate-level phosphorylation is as follows:

In glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm, a gross total of $4$ ATP molecules are synthesized during the payoff phase. However, $2$ ATP molecules are consumed during the initial preparatory phase, leaving a net gain of $2$ ATP molecules.

In the Krebs cycle, which takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, $1$ GTP molecule (equivalent to $1$ ATP) is generated directly per turn during the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate. Since one molecule of glucose gives rise to two molecules of acetyl-CoA, the Krebs cycle operates twice per glucose molecule, resulting in the production of $2$ ATP molecules.

Summing up the net contributions from both stages, the total number of net ATP molecules formed through substrate-level phosphorylation is:
$2\text{ (from glycolysis)} + 2\text{ (from Krebs cycle)} = 4\text{ ATP}$

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A female gametophyte of an angiospermic plant is developed from a megaspore mother cell by ------------------.
options: one meiotic and two mitotic divisions
one meiotic and three mitotic divisions
two meiotic and two mitotic divisions
three meiotic and one mitotic divisions
questions.solution:
The megaspore mother cell (MMC) in the ovule undergoes one meiotic division to produce four haploid megaspores.

Out of these four megaspores, usually three degenerate and only one remains functional.

The functional megaspore then undergoes three successive free-nuclear mitotic divisions.

The first mitotic division produces a $2$-nucleate stage, the second produces a $4$-nucleate stage, and the third produces an $8$-nucleate stage.

These $8$ nuclei eventually organize into the typical $7$-celled, $8$-nucleate female gametophyte (embryo sac).

Thus, the entire process requires one meiotic division and three mitotic divisions.

Answer: one meiotic and three mitotic divisions

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: All of the following aquatic plants are entomophilous EXCEPT
questions.solution:
In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth, water lily, and lotus, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind. These plants are entomophilous or anemophilous.

Vallisneria is a submerged dioecious aquatic plant where pollination occurs on the surface of water. The female flower reaches the surface of water by a long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released onto the surface of water. They are carried passively by water currents. This type of pollination is known as epihydrophily.

Therefore, Vallisneria is not entomophilous.

Answer: Vallisneria

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Outbreeding device)		List II
(example)
(A). Unisexuality(I). Gloriosa
(B). Protandry(II). Mulberry
(C). Protogyny(III). Apple
(D). Prepotency(IV). Disc florets of sunflower
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Unisexuality is the condition where flowers are either male or female. Mulberry is an example of a plant with unisexual flowers.

Protandry is a condition where the anthers mature earlier than the stigma of the same flower. Disc florets of sunflower exhibit protandry.

Protogyny is a condition where the stigma matures earlier than the anthers. Gloriosa is an example of a plant exhibiting protogyny.

Prepotency is the phenomenon where pollen from a different flower germinates faster on the stigma than pollen from the same flower. Apple is an example of prepotency.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which is NOT a common example of adventive polyembryony?
questions.solution:
Adventive polyembryony is the formation of additional embryos from the diploid sporophytic cells of the ovule, such as the nucellus or integuments, outside the embryo sac.

Common examples of adventive polyembryony include Citrus species (like orange and lemon) and mango.

Pineapple does not exhibit adventive polyembryony; it is typically parthenocarpic and is propagated vegetatively.

Thus, pineapple is not a common example of adventive polyembryony.

Answer: Pineapple

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which type of apomixis, a haploid embryo sac produces a haploid embryo from an egg or any other haploid cell of gametophyte?
questions.solution:
In non-recurrent apomixis, the megaspore mother cell undergoes normal meiosis to form a haploid embryo sac. The embryo develops either from the haploid egg cell (haploid parthenogenesis) or from any other haploid cell of the embryo sac (haploid apogamy) without fertilization. The resulting plants are haploid and generally sterile.

In recurrent apomixis, the embryo sac is diploid and the embryo develops from a diploid cell.

In diplospory, the embryo sac develops directly from the megaspore mother cell without meiosis, resulting in a diploid embryo sac.

In adventive polyembryony, embryos develop directly from diploid sporophytic cells such as the nucellus or integument.

Answer: Non-recurrent apomixis

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: If the synergid of an ovule contains 24 chromosomes, then what will be the number of chromosomes in its endosperm?
questions.solution:
Synergids are haploid cells present in the embryo sac of an angiosperm.

Thus, the haploid chromosome number is $n = 24$.

The endosperm in angiosperms is formed by triple fusion and is typically triploid ($3n$).

Number of chromosomes in the endosperm = $3n = 3 \times 24 = 72$.

Answer: $72$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Disease resistant, high-yielding variety of rice developed by mutation breeding is -----------.
questions.solution:
Mutation breeding is a technique used to develop improved crop varieties by inducing mutations.

Jagannath is a high-yielding, semi-dwarf variety of rice developed through mutation breeding using X-rays on the tall variety T-141.

NP 836 is a mutant variety of wheat resistant to rust.

Regina-II is a mutant variety of cabbage.

Indore-2 is a mutant variety of cotton.

Answer: Jagannath

questions.subject: Biology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q:

List I
(Source of SCP)		List II
(Example)
(A). Fungi(I). Chlorella pyrenoidosa
(B). Yeast(II). Methylophilus methylotropus
(C). Algae(III). Candida utilis
(D). Bacteria(IV). Aspergillus niger
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Single Cell Protein (SCP) is obtained from various microorganisms.

Fungi: Aspergillus niger is a filamentous fungus used as a source of SCP. Thus, (A) matches with (IV).

Yeast: Candida utilis (also known as Torula yeast) is a widely used yeast for SCP production. Thus, (B) matches with (III).

Algae: Chlorella pyrenoidosa is a unicellular green alga rich in proteins. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

Answer: (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: If any solute is added in pure water, what will be the effect on the value of water potential?
options: Value of water potential is increased.
Value of water potential is decreased.
There is no change in its value.
Value of water potential becomes more than D.P.D.
questions.solution:
Pure water has the maximum water potential, which is zero at standard temperature and pressure.

When a solute is added to pure water, the concentration of free water molecules decreases, which lowers the free energy of water.

This results in a decrease in the water potential, making it negative.

Therefore, the value of water potential is decreased.

Answer: Value of water potential is decreased.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Select the correct statement from the following.
options: In a fully turgid cell, TP = OP.
In a fully turgid cell, TP > OP.
In a fully turgid cell, DPD = OP.
Turgor pressure decreases when the cell is placed in hypotonic solution.
questions.solution:
The diffusion pressure deficit (DPD) of a cell is given by the relation DPD = OP - TP, where OP is the osmotic pressure and TP is the turgor pressure.

When a cell is fully turgid, it cannot absorb any more water, which means its DPD becomes zero.

Substituting DPD = 0 in the equation, we get 0 = OP - TP, which implies OP = TP.

When a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution, water enters the cell due to endosmosis, causing the turgor pressure to increase, not decrease.

Answer: In a fully turgid cell, TP = OP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which is the driving force for the process of passive absorption of water in roots?
questions.solution:
Passive absorption of water by roots is driven by the transpiration pull created in the leaves. As water evaporates from the stomata during transpiration, a negative pressure or tension develops in the xylem vessels of the leaves. This tension is transmitted downwards through the continuous water column in the xylem to the roots, creating a suction force that pulls water from the soil into the root hairs. Root pressure, on the other hand, is an active process.

Answer: Transpiration pull in leaves

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Types of translocation)		List II
(Path of translocation)
(A). Radial translocation(I). From leaves to growing point of stem
(B). Tangential translocation(II). From phloem to pith
(C). Upward translocation(III). From leaves to roots
(D). Downward translocation(IV). From phloem to cortex
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Radial translocation is the lateral movement of organic solutes from the phloem to the pith.

Tangential translocation is the lateral movement of organic solutes from the phloem to the cortex.

Upward translocation is the movement of synthesized food from the leaves to the growing points of the stem, developing flowers, and fruits.

Downward translocation is the movement of synthesized food from the leaves to the roots for utilization and storage.

Thus, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is found in Indian gooseberry?
questions.solution:
Indian gooseberry, also known as Amla, is a rich source of Vitamin C and various polyphenols, including gallic acid, ellagic acid, and corilagin.

Curcumin is the active ingredient found in turmeric.

Eugenol is the main component of clove oil.

Methyl salicylate is commonly found in wintergreen oil.

Therefore, gallic acid is the compound found in Indian gooseberry.

Answer: Gallic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Butan-2-ol is heated with red phosphorous and bromine. Find the number of optical isomers of the product formed.
questions.solution:
The reaction of butan-2-ol with red phosphorus and bromine yields 2-bromobutane.

$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3 \xrightarrow{P/Br_2} CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_3$

The product, 2-bromobutane, contains exactly one chiral carbon atom (the second carbon is attached to four different groups: $-H$, $-Br$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH_2CH_3$).

The number of optical isomers for a compound with $n$ dissimilar chiral centers is given by $2^n$.

For $n = 1$, the number of optical isomers is $2^1 = 2$. These correspond to the (R) and (S) enantiomers.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound A on reaction with thionyl chloride, gives compound B. Compound B, reacts with sodium in dry ether as solvent, gives 2,3-dimethyl butane. Identify compound A.
questions.solution:
Compound B reacts with sodium in dry ether to give 2,3-dimethylbutane. This is a Wurtz reaction.

$2R-Cl + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-R + 2NaCl$

Since the product $R-R$ is 2,3-dimethylbutane, $(CH_3)_2CH-CH(CH_3)_2$, the alkyl group $R$ must be an isopropyl group, $(CH_3)_2CH-$.

Therefore, compound B is isopropyl chloride, $(CH_3)_2CH-Cl$.

Compound A reacts with thionyl chloride ($SOCl_2$) to give compound B. This indicates that compound A is an alcohol.

$R-OH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow R-Cl + SO_2 + HCl$

Thus, compound A is isopropyl alcohol, $(CH_3)_2CH-OH$.

Answer: Isopropyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following reagents convert propene to 1-propanol?
questions.solution:
Propene is $CH_3-CH=CH_2$.

Conversion of propene to 1-propanol ($CH_3-CH_2-CH_2OH$) involves the anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond.

Hydroboration-oxidation is the standard method for anti-Markovnikov hydration of alkenes.

The reagents used are diborane ($B_2H_6$) followed by hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$) in an alkaline medium ($OH^-$).

Reaction:
$3CH_3-CH=CH_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}B_2H_6 \rightarrow (CH_3-CH_2-CH_2)_3B$

$(CH_3-CH_2-CH_2)_3B + 3H_2O_2 \xrightarrow{OH^-} 3CH_3-CH_2-CH_2OH + H_3BO_3$

Acid-catalyzed hydration ($H_2O, H_2SO_4$) yields 2-propanol (Markovnikov addition).

Cold alkaline $KMnO_4$ yields propane-1,2-diol.

Therefore, $B_2H_6, H_2O_2, OH^-$ is the correct reagent.

Answer: $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6, \text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{OH}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product when propan-2-ol heated with Cu at $573$ K.
questions.solution:
Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol.

When a secondary alcohol is heated with copper at $573$ K, it undergoes dehydrogenation to form a ketone.

$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{Cu, 573 K} CH_3-CO-CH_3 + H_2$

The product formed is propanone.

Answer: Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound 'A' on oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate forms an aldehyde having the molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$. What is compound 'A'?
questions.solution:
The aldehyde with the molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ is ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

Since the product is a two-carbon aldehyde (ethanal), the reactant 'A' must be a two-carbon primary alcohol.

Therefore, compound 'A' is ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$).

The reaction is: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$

Answer: Ethanol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the product formed on the reduction of carboxylic acids using lithium aluminum hydride?
questions.solution:
Lithium aluminum hydride ($LiAlH_4$) is a strong reducing agent.

It reduces carboxylic acids directly to primary alcohols.

The general reaction is:
$R-COOH \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} R-CH_2OH$

Thus, the product formed is a primary alcohol.

Answer: Primary alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compounds, on reaction with hydrogen cyanide (HCN), gives an optically active cyanohydrin?
questions.solution:
Reaction of a carbonyl compound with $\text{HCN}$ yields a cyanohydrin.

For the cyanohydrin to be optically active, the carbon atom formed from the carbonyl carbon must be chiral, meaning it must be bonded to four different groups.

For $\text{CH}_3\text{-COCH}_3$, the cyanohydrin is $\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)(CN)-CH}_3$, which has two identical methyl groups and is achiral.

For $\text{H-CHO}$, the cyanohydrin is $\text{H-C(OH)(CN)-H}$, which has two identical hydrogen atoms and is achiral.

For $\text{CH}_3\text{-CHO}$, the cyanohydrin is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)(CN)}$, which has four different groups ($\text{CH}_3$, $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CN}$) attached to the central carbon. It is chiral and optically active.

For $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-C}_6\text{H}_5$, the cyanohydrin is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-C(OH)(CN)-C}_6\text{H}_5$, which has two identical phenyl groups and is achiral.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CHO}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzaldehyde is converted to benzyl alcohol by
questions.solution:
Benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5CHO$) is an aldehyde that does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom.

When treated with a concentrated alkali solution, it undergoes a disproportionation reaction (self-oxidation and self-reduction) to form one molecule of benzyl alcohol ($C_6H_5CH_2OH$) and one molecule of a salt of benzoic acid ($C_6H_5COO^-$).

This reaction is known as Cannizzaro's reaction.

$2C_6H_5CHO + NaOH \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_2OH + C_6H_5COONa$

Wurtz, Fittig, and Wurtz-Fittig reactions are coupling reactions involving alkyl and/or aryl halides in the presence of sodium metal.

Answer: Cannizzaro's reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following methods is the most convenient method to prepare an amine containing one carbon atom less than the parent compound?
questions.solution:
Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction is used for the preparation of primary amines from primary amides. In this reaction, a primary amide is treated with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide.

The general reaction is given by:
$R-CONH_2 + Br_2 + 4NaOH \rightarrow R-NH_2 + Na_2CO_3 + 2NaBr + 2H_2O$

The resulting primary amine contains one carbon atom less than the parent amide due to the loss of the carbonyl carbon as sodium carbonate. Thus, it is the most convenient method to prepare an amine containing one carbon atom less than the parent compound.

Answer: Hofmann bromamide reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements regarding biological importance of elements is NOT true?
options: $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions are required for contraction and stretching of muscles.
$\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions are important for breaking of glucose and fats in protein synthesis.
$\text{K}^{+}$ ions are most abundant in extra cellular fluid.
$\text{Na}^{+}$ ions regulate water flow across the membrane.
questions.solution:
Sodium ions ($\text{Na}^{+}$) are the most abundant cations in the extracellular fluid (blood plasma and interstitial fluid), whereas potassium ions ($\text{K}^{+}$) are the most abundant cations in the intracellular fluid (within cell fluids).

Therefore, the statement that $\text{K}^{+}$ ions are most abundant in extracellular fluid is incorrect.

Answer: $\text{K}^{+}$ ions are most abundant in extra cellular fluid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of following peptides, the glycylalanine is?
questions.solution:
Glycylalanine is formed by the condensation of two amino acids, glycine and alanine, linked by a single peptide bond.

Since it contains exactly two amino acid residues, it is classified as a dipeptide.

Answer: Dipeptide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does fructose reduce Fehling's solution?
options: Due to the presence of hydroxy group.
Due to the presence of aldehydic group
Due to the presence of ketonic group.
Due to the presence of alpha-hydroxy ketonic group
questions.solution:
Fructose is a monosaccharide containing a ketonic group at the second carbon and hydroxyl groups on adjacent carbons, making it an $\alpha$-hydroxy ketone.

Under the alkaline conditions of Fehling's solution, fructose undergoes Lobry de Bruyn-van Ekenstein rearrangement.

This rearrangement converts the $\alpha$-hydroxy ketone into an enediol intermediate, which further tautomerizes into an aldose (a mixture of glucose and mannose).

The newly formed aldehydic group then readily reduces Fehling's solution.

Thus, fructose reduces Fehling's solution due to the presence of the $\alpha$-hydroxy ketonic group.

Answer: Due to the presence of alpha-hydroxy ketonic group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species is paramagnetic?
questions.solution:
The magnetic nature of a species can be determined by its molecular orbital electronic configuration.

For $\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} = \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2}$. All electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic.

For $\text{Li}_2$ (6 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2}$. All electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic.

For $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} = \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi^{*}_{2p_x}^{2} = \pi^{*}_{2p_y}^{2}$. All electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic.

For $\text{N}_2^{+}$ (13 electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} = \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{1}$. It has one unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic.

Answer: $\text{N}_2^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following ligands is present in a metal carbonyl complex?
questions.solution:
Metal carbonyl complexes are coordination compounds in which transition metals are bonded to carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) ligands.

Therefore, the ligand present in a metal carbonyl complex is $\text{CO}$.

Answer: $\text{CO}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name of $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$?
questions.solution:
The given coordination compound is $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$.

The cation is potassium and the complex anion is $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$.

Let the oxidation state of iron (Fe) be $x$.

The charge on each cyanide (CN) ligand is $-1$.

Equating the sum of oxidation states to the charge on the complex ion:

$x + 6(-1) = -3$

$x - 6 = -3$

$x = +3$

The complex anion contains six cyanide ligands, which are named as 'hexacyano'.

Since the complex is an anion, the suffix '-ate' is added to the Latin name of iron, making it 'ferrate'.

The oxidation state is written in Roman numerals in parentheses as (III).

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name is Potassium hexacyanoferrate(III).

Answer: Potassium hexacyanoferrate(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is standard decrease in Gibbs energy for the following cell?
$\text{Al}_{(s)} \mid \text{Al}^{+3}_{(1M)} \parallel \text{Cd}^{+2}_{(1M)} \mid \text{Cd}$
if $E^\circ\,\text{Al}^{+3}/\text{Al} = -1.66$ V, $E^\circ\,\text{Cd}^{+2}/\text{Cd} = -0.40$ V
questions.solution:
The standard cell potential is given by:

$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$

$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.40 - (-1.66) = 1.26 \text{ V}$

The half-cell reactions are:

Anode: $\text{Al} \rightarrow \text{Al}^{+3} + 3e^-$

Cathode: $\text{Cd}^{+2} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Cd}$

To balance the number of electrons, the overall reaction involves the transfer of $6$ electrons, so $n = 6$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is:

$\Delta G^\circ = -n F E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$

$\Delta G^\circ = -6 \times 96500 \times 1.26$

$\Delta G^\circ = -729540 \text{ J} = -729.54 \text{ kJ}$

Answer: $-729.54$ kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct order of increasing reducing strength of metals from following.
questions.solution:
Reducing strength of a metal depends on its tendency to lose electrons, which is inversely proportional to its standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}$).

A lower (more negative) standard reduction potential indicates a stronger reducing agent.

The standard reduction potentials ($E^{\circ}$) for the given metals are:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Li}^{+} / \text{Li}} = -3.05 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Mg}^{2+} / \text{Mg}} = -2.36 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Ni}^{2+} / \text{Ni}} = -0.25 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{Ag}^{+} / \text{Ag}} = +0.80 \text{ V}$

Since the reduction potential increases in the order $\text{Li} \lt \text{Mg} \lt \text{Ni} \lt \text{Ag}$, the reducing strength increases in the reverse order.

Thus, the correct order of increasing reducing strength is $\text{Ag} \lt \text{Ni} \lt \text{Mg} \lt \text{Li}$.

Answer: Ag < Ni < Mg < Li

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the molar conductivity of $0.001$M $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution if the conductivity of it is $1.2 \times 10^{-4}\Omega^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Given:

Concentration, $M = 0.001 \text{ M}$

Conductivity, $\kappa = 1.2 \times 10^{-4} \ \Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

The formula for molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{M}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.001}$

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10^{-1}}{10^{-3}}$

$\Lambda_m = 1.2 \times 10^2$

$\Lambda_m = 120 \ \Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to green chemistry, which of the following features is NOT favored by the catalyst?
questions.solution:
According to the principles of green chemistry, the use of catalysts is highly encouraged because they lower the activation energy, which reduces energy demands and reaction times. Catalysts also improve the selectivity of a reaction, leading to a higher yield of the desired product.

Green chemistry aims to minimize or eliminate the generation of hazardous substances and waste. Therefore, an increase in waste is contrary to the goals of green chemistry and is not a favored feature of a catalyst.

Answer: Increase in waste

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following formula of the third higher Homologue of $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$?
questions.solution:
Homologous series members differ by a successive $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit.

The given compound is propanoic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

The first higher homologue is obtained by adding one $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

The second higher homologue is obtained by adding two $-\text{CH}_2-$ units: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

The third higher homologue is obtained by adding three $-\text{CH}_2-$ units: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl halides gives a mixture of alkenes on dehydrohalogenation?
questions.solution:
Dehydrohalogenation of alkyl halides involves the removal of a hydrogen atom from a $\beta$-carbon and a halogen atom from the $\alpha$-carbon to form an alkene.

For n-propyl bromide ($CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Br$), there is only one $\beta$-carbon, yielding only propene.

For isopropyl bromide ($CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3$), the two $\beta$-carbons are equivalent, yielding only propene.

For secondary butyl bromide ($CH_3-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$), there are two non-equivalent $\beta$-carbons. Elimination of hydrogen from these different $\beta$-carbons yields a mixture of 1-butene and 2-butene (which further exists as cis and trans isomers).

For tertiary butyl bromide ($(CH_3)_3C-Br$), all three $\beta$-carbons are equivalent, yielding only 2-methylpropene.

Thus, secondary butyl bromide gives a mixture of alkenes.

Answer: Secondary butyl bromide

questions.solution:
The given reaction shows the conversion of benzenediazonium chloride ($C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-$) to chlorobenzene ($C_6H_5Cl$) using copper(I) chloride ($Cu_2Cl_2$) as a reagent.

This is a classic example of the Sandmeyer reaction, where an aryl diazonium group is replaced by a halide or pseudohalide (like $Cl^-$, $Br^-$, or $CN^-$) in the presence of the corresponding copper(I) salt.

Other reactions mentioned:
Fittig reaction involves the coupling of two aryl halides using sodium metal.
Kolbe reaction is the carboxylation of sodium phenoxide to form salicylic acid.
Reimer-Tiemann reaction is the formylation of phenol using chloroform and a base to form salicylaldehyde.

Answer: Sandmeyer reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the products when benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of (I) Fe and (II) anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ respectively from the following.
questions.solution:
Benzene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution when it reacts with halogens in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst.

In the first case, iron ($\text{Fe}$) reacts with chlorine to form $\text{FeCl}_3$ in situ, which acts as a Lewis acid. It facilitates the generation of the electrophile ($\text{Cl}^+$), leading to the formation of chlorobenzene.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Fe}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$

In the second case, anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is also a Lewis acid and similarly catalyzes the electrophilic substitution of benzene with chlorine to yield chlorobenzene.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$

Note: Hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$) is formed only when benzene reacts with an *excess* of chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in the dark. Since excess chlorine is not mentioned, monosubstitution is considered for both reactions.

Therefore, the product in both cases (I) and (II) is chlorobenzene.
